name: Pierre Trudeau
summary: Trudeau, Justice Minister and Prime Minister, decriminalised private adult conduct in his 1967 Omnibus Bill, invoked the War Measures Act against the FLQ in 1970, defended federalism against Quebec separatism and brought home the Constitution with a Charter of Rights in 1982.

sources.title: 'No place for the state in the bedrooms of the nation' (CBC Archives, 21 February 1967 clip of Justice Minister Trudeau on his Omnibus Bill, with CBC's 2018 write-up)
sources.author: CBC News
sources.usedFor: Direct quotation: 'What's done in private between adults doesn't concern the Criminal Code'; the bill's abortion, lottery and gun provisions

sources.title: 'Just watch me': When Pierre Trudeau confronted the October Crisis (CBC Archives, 2018)
sources.author: CBC News
sources.usedFor: He invoked the War Measures Act on 16 October 1970, letting police arrest and detain on suspicion alone, and outlawed the FLQ

sources.title: Pierre Trudeau, address to the nation on the October Crisis, 16 October 1970 (Great Canadian Speeches)
sources.author: Pierre Elliott Trudeau
sources.usedFor: His case that democracy must defend itself against 'violent and fanatical men' when 'an effective mechanism to change governments by peaceful means' exists

sources.title: Federal-Provincial Conference of First Ministers on the Constitution, transcript of the Prime Minister's statement, 8 September 1980 (PrimaryDocuments.ca, Doc 800-14/050)
sources.author: Pierre Elliott Trudeau
sources.usedFor: Says Canada is already 'the most decentralized federation in the world' and what is sought is 'a renewed federalism'

sources.title: Pierre Elliott Trudeau, statement on multiculturalism to the House of Commons, 8 October 1971 (transcription, canadahistory.ca; House of Commons Debates, 28th Parl, 3rd Sess, vol. 8)
sources.author: Pierre Elliott Trudeau
sources.usedFor: Announcing multiculturalism within a bilingual framework: no official culture, no ethnic group takes precedence, government support for the various cultures

sources.title: Constitution Act, 1982, Part I: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms (text, Justice Laws Website; patriated and enacted under Prime Minister Trudeau)
sources.author: Parliament of Canada / UK Parliament
sources.usedFor: Sections 1-33: fundamental freedoms, equality (s.15), official languages and minority-language education (ss.16-23), jury trial (s.11(f)), the equal rights of male and female persons (s.28), the notwithstanding clause (s.33)

sources.title: Revised Statutes of Canada 1970, Criminal Code (c. C-34, vol. 2), as amended by the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1968-69 (c. 38) that Trudeau introduced as Justice Minister (Internet Archive revisedstatutes197002uoft)
sources.author: Parliament of Canada
sources.usedFor: s.158 (private acts of consenting adults exempt from the gross-indecency and buggery offences), s.251(4) (therapeutic abortion committees), ss.82-106 (restricted weapons registration)

sources.title: Wage and Price Controls (The Canadian Encyclopedia, Ronald G. Wirick; Wayback copy)
sources.author: The Canadian Encyclopedia
sources.usedFor: The federal Anti-Inflation Act of 1975 set up a three-year controls system with binding wage guidelines and profit-margin controls

sources.title: Petro-Canada (The Canadian Encyclopedia; Wayback copy)
sources.author: The Canadian Encyclopedia
sources.usedFor: Trudeau's government accepted an NDP motion in 1973 and passed the Petro-Canada Act in 1975 creating a Crown oil company over which Ottawa kept authority of its budget and strategy

notFound.work: Trudeau's speeches and debates in the House of Commons 1968-84, his Memoirs (1993) and Federalism and the French Canadians (1968)

public-ownership.rationale: His government created Petro-Canada by statute in 1975 as a Crown corporation with broad powers in exploration, refining and marketing; a single state oil company, not major industries generally.

limit-guns.rationale: The 1968-69 Act he introduced made restricted weapons (handguns, short or rapid-fire firearms) subject to registration certificates and tightened permits (Criminal Code ss.82-106).

decide-locally.rationale: Told the 1980 first ministers' conference that 'we are living in the most decentralized federation in the world', that the provinces already have 'enormous power', and that what is sought is 'a renewed federalism, an improved division of powers'.

abortion-legal.rationale: The 1968-69 Act he introduced made abortion lawful in an accredited hospital only if a therapeutic abortion committee certifies that continuing the pregnancy would or would likely endanger the woman's life or health (Criminal Code s.251(4)): decriminalised in narrow cases, not in most.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Petro-Canada was created in 1975 as the government's 'policy arm', with Ottawa holding authority over its capital budget and strategy and a mandate to develop frontier oil sands, Arctic and offshore resources.

harm-principle.rationale: As Justice Minister he introduced the 1968-69 Criminal Law Amendment Act whose s.158 exempts from the buggery and gross-indecency offences any act committed in private between two persons of twenty-one or over who consent, and said 'there's no place for the state in the bedrooms of the nation'.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Announced in 1971 that 'the government will support and encourage the various cultures and ethnic groups that give structure and vitality to our society', since 'the individual's freedom would be hampered if he were locked for life within a particular cultural compartment' while every Canadian should be able to learn one of the two official languages.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Charter he drove through, s.15(1): 'Every individual is equal before and under the law and has the right to the equal protection and equal benefit of the law without discrimination'.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Under the War Measures Act in October 1970 his government outlawed the FLQ, the separatist group that kidnapped James Cross and Pierre Laporte (a terrorist group, not a party contesting elections).

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: On 16 October 1970 he invoked the War Measures Act in peacetime, giving police the right to arrest and detain people on suspicion alone, to put down the FLQ's kidnappings.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Told the House of Commons in 1971: 'although there are two official languages, there is no official culture, nor does any ethnic group take precedence over any other. No citizen or group of citizens is other than Canadian, and all should be treated fairly.'

minority-language-support.rationale: The Charter he entrenched gives English and French equal status in federal institutions (ss.16-20), guarantees minority-language educational rights (s.23) and requires interpretation consistent with the multicultural heritage of Canadians (s.27).

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: As Prime Minister he drove the Constitution Act 1982, entrenching the Charter of Rights and Freedoms in the constitution as 'the supreme law', though s.33 lets Parliament or a legislature override most rights for five years.

single-official-language.rationale: The Charter he entrenched, s.16(1): 'English and French are the official languages of Canada and have equality of status', with minority-language education rights in s.23.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Charter he entrenched gives every citizen the right to vote (s.3) and s.28 guarantees its rights 'equally to male and female persons'.

constitutional-jury-trial.rationale: Charter s.11(f), part of the Constitution Act 1982 he drove, guarantees 'the benefit of trial by jury' for offences carrying five years or more, except under military law.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: His government's Anti-Inflation Act of 1975 set up a three-year system of binding wage guidelines and profit-margin controls to fight inflation.

notes: Deeper pass: acts added from the Constitution Act 1982 (Charter), the Criminal Code as amended 1968-69 (Revised Statutes 1970), and tier-3 reports of the Anti-Inflation Act and Petro-Canada Act (Canadian Encyclopedia, Wayback copies): thirteen more answers, all record. Not found: Official Languages Act 1969 text (searched the RSC 1970 volumes: not located), National Energy Program text, lipad.ca Commons Hansard (403, final), his 14 May 1980 referendum speech (not located). First pass: eight answers from the CBC archive pages, his October Crisis address and his 1980 first ministers' statement. The 1971 multiculturalism statement (canadahistory.ca transcription) adds cultures-equal-different +2 high, assimilate-immigrants -2 medium, minority-language-support +1 medium. Not answered: right-to-secede (only a one-line 2000 CNN clip, 'the place of Quebec is in Canada', without context), national-self-determination. A deeper pass could use his Memoirs (not local) and the Charter debates. Failing the uncertainty rule is the expected outcome.
